summary: Implemented selective FP8 KV dequantization for eager BF16 DSA sparse prefill. The path translates ragged logical top-k positions to physical cache slots, deduplicates shared/overlapping slots, dequantizes the union once, remaps top-k indices to the compact BF16 buffer, and falls back to full-prefix dequantization below a conservative measured crossover gate.

tests.what_was_measured: Three MI350X GPU tests: exact independent FP8-pack/BF16-dequant numerical reconstruction, physical alias deduplication and remapping with duplicate/multi-request/-1 inputs, short-prefix fallback compatibility, and invalid/all-empty sentinel handling. 3 passed.

Actual MI350X Triton execution at 262144 logical rows, 8 query rows and top-k 2048: 4029 compact physical rows; BF16 staging 301989888 to 4641408 bytes; full 0.7931 ms versus selective 0.3013 ms (2.632x). Earlier retained investigation found 32768 rows regressed, motivating the 131072-row default floor.
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, syntax, registered-test manifest, and policy hooks all passed.

Attempted real DSA backend coverage on MI350X. Result: 1 passed, 4 skipped, 2 failed before attention execution because the prepared HIP legacy DSA path requires page_size == 1 while the fixture uses page_size 64. Raw traceback retained.

gpu_evidence: New Triton dequantization and torch.unique/remap code executed numerically and under timing on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950); raw pytest and benchmark logs are retained in this report directory.
remaining_limitations: The requested BF16 flashmla_sparse attention kernel is NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell-only and cannot execute on the assigned AMD MI350X. End-to-end sparse-attention output remains unverified on its target architecture; only the selective mapping/dequantization stage has independent GPU numerical validation here.
The existing DSA FP8 prefill fixture cannot reach attention on this HIP environment because its page_size=64 conflicts with the legacy HIP DSA requirement page_size==1.

The 131072-row crossover floor is conservative and calibrated on the assigned MI350X. The related upstream draft reports a lower H20 crossover, but this contribution does not claim an independently measured NVIDIA threshold or end-to-end model performance.
No full DeepSeek model weights or qualified architecture-matching serving fixture were available; transport/startup smoke would not validate this kernel feature and was therefore not substituted.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
